controls_available: Difficulty 4 uses a 9x9 board, 5 solution arrows, at most 6 placed arrows, 18 beats, and a 260 ms beat interval; the event, wall, beat, and collision minimums constrain generated-task richness.

In simplified interaction, click an empty grid square to arm it, press ADD to place an up arrow, select a placed arrow, and press ROTATE to cycle its direction. These configuration edits are available only in edit phase.

RUN FILM starts the 18-beat film; STEP ONE BEAT advances one beat only in response to an agent action; CLEAR CONFIGURATION resets the board; REVISE STARTING ARROWS becomes available after a film; CHECK SEQUENCE is the final administrative submission.
The configured observation bound is a 600 ms window with 5 chronological frames, and the play allowance is 120 seconds.
autonomous_processes: While the board is in edit phase, waiting produces no task-state progression; the target, configuration, and available edit controls remain stable.

After RUN FILM, beat 1 is applied synchronously and each later beat is applied autonomously by a 260 ms timer until beat 18. Arrows move one square, reverse on wall impacts, turn clockwise on occupied or duplicate destinations, and append visibly flashing wall events to the ledger.

Wall-flash removal timers and CSS movement/flash transitions settle without agent actions, but they are display effects and do not change the replayed outcome or create an expiring control opportunity.
STEP ONE BEAT is action-triggered rather than autonomous; post-film submission and failure-state UI updates are administrative.
grouped_control_modes: All simplified placement occurrences using the ADD control after an empty-square selection (input source add_button).
All simplified direction-edit occurrences using ROTATE on a selected arrow (input source cycle_button).
All film-start occurrences using RUN FILM (run-film).
All manual progression occurrences using STEP ONE BEAT (step-beat).
All configuration reset/revision occurrences using CLEAR CONFIGURATION or REVISE STARTING ARROWS.
CHECK SEQUENCE is administrative certification and is not an outcome-affecting control mode.

clause_i.reason: For the legitimate pre-film configuration-edit mode, an observation-free q sees only I_t and cannot condition the target-dependent placement or direction on the seed-specific visible target across histories. The target and current board can instead determine the next edit. This is a static planning dependency, not a real-time witness.

clause_ii.reason: The complete target wall ledger and current configuration are visible in the task UI and persist during editing. A bounded current screenshot, including the endpoint of the configured 600 ms/5-frame observation window, is sufficient in principle to choose a target-directed edit; no unbounded temporal memory is required for that choice.

clause_iii.reason: The only autonomous task-state evolution is the post-RUN film, but while phase is running the ADD, ROTATE, RUN, STEP, CLEAR, and REVISE controls are disabled or ignored. No outcome-affecting action remains available whose value can strictly decrease during the film. Waiting in edit phase does not start the film, and STEP changes the state only after a new agent action. A later-enabled REVISE or CHECK action is an enabling-after-wait case, which the definition excludes. Therefore no legitimate D, Delta, and common visible process repairs clause (iii).

common_visible_process: The 18-beat arrow film is visibly changing: the grid updates, wall rails flash at side/slot positions, and the observed ledger accumulates beat-indexed events. It is not a common real-time witness because all edits happen before the film, the edit/revision controls are unavailable during it, and the ledger remains available for later revision rather than expiring.

pre_run.reason: generate() always returns a fixed solution list from _find_candidate (including its deterministic fallback) and constructs target_events by simulating that list for the configured board and beats. The simplified controls can reproduce the solution before RUN; the solver configures it, waits for the film to complete, and submits only afterward. This establishes a successful pre-run construction for every generated instance structurally, without treating the solver's private truth access as policy information.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 4 is the hard 9x9, 5-arrow, 6-max-cell, 18-beat, 260 ms configuration with the specified generation thresholds.
Simplified interaction uses square selection plus ADD and ROTATE, while the observation settings are 120 seconds, 600 ms, and 5 frames.
The runtime preserves the selected materialized difficulty and interaction condition and changes only the live/paused clock mode.

The visible task describes one-square motion, wall reversal, clockwise encounters, an event ledger, and edits before the film; the source note explicitly distinguishes changing-frame observation from a non-expiring correct edit.
The simulation advances all arrows beat by beat, records wall side/slot events, reverses on walls, and turns on occupied or duplicate destinations.
Every generated task obtains a solution list or fallback and sets the target event sequence to the simulation of that list; the same contract is exposed publicly and stored as truth.
The simplified UI records ADD and ROTATE edit events, binds square/arrow clicks, and renders the target sequence and proxy controls visibly.
The film changes simulation state, flashes wall events, applies beat 1 on RUN, and schedules later beats autonomously at beat_ms intervals through completion.
Manual stepping requires an action, revision is post-film, and updateControls disables edit, run, step, revision, and submission controls in the running phase as appropriate.
The board, moving cells, wall rails, flashing hit slots, persistent target/event ledgers, and non-task failure/pass animations are visible presentation elements.
The grader binds expected input sources to simplified/full interaction, replays the fixed cells for all requested beats, and accepts only a matching wall-event outcome.
Verification loads the exported result and independently invokes the Collision Chimes grader; it adds no alternate timing mechanic.
The simplified solver uses the visible proxy controls, waits for phase complete after configuration, and only then submits, providing the pre-run execution pattern.
